market_holds: Spot $88.85 at the 2026-11-17 close (sealed baseline): +8.6% over 20 sessions, -0.6% over 5, 9.7% below the 52-week high. The Earnings Whispers preview (2026-11-10) puts the stock up 10.7% since the Q3 print while the S&P fell about 3%. No usable option chain (ATM spread 140% of mid), so the expected move is the median of 7 prior reactions, 7.0% (+7.66 Aug-26, -7.01 May-26, -15.44 Feb-26, +1.13 Nov-25). Consensus FQ4 EPS is $1.21 on $400.5M revenue (-2.4% y/y vs $410.2M), from about 3 analysts (StoneX, Jefferies, William Blair, all Buy, last actions 2026-08-05/06). The FY26 EPS consensus of $3.93, set after Q3, less the reported Q1-Q3 adjusted $0.33+$0.40+$1.96 implies Q4 about $1.24, so the $1.21 reflects the post-Q3 view and is about 100 days old. There is no formal guide. On the Q3 call management said bakery SKU drag shrinks from about 3.5% to 2.5% of sales in Q4, new churro, SuperPretzel QSR and novelty business starts shipping, beverage volume partly offsets machine/service declines, freight and fuel persist into Q4 (Q3 net hit $4.7M), Apollo savings run ahead (target at least $25M), and growth returns in FY27. Short interest is about 5-6% of float (latest dated figure 5.11% on 2026-04-30). Earnings Whispers calls sentiment bearish but softening and expectations risen.
view: This is a stabilisation quarter. The stock trades on whether Apollo margin gains outrun freight and whether the sales decline keeps narrowing toward FY27 growth. The Q3 rally (+7.7%) came from a margin beat, and the Feb and May sell-offs came from sales and demand commentary while EPS matched. My own rebuild puts FQ4 adjusted EPS around $1.25-1.50 against $1.21. Apollo was not in last year's Q4. Diesel's year-on-year increase in Jul-Sep (+$1.68/gal) is about the same as in Q3 (+$1.86), so the freight hit should be close to Q3's $4.7M, which is already in the guide. The $1.58 year-ago base was flattered by a 4.8% effective tax rate and some business-interruption insurance, which is why the consensus sits 23% below it. So a modest EPS beat is more likely than a miss, in line with this analyst group under-calling Apollo by $0.15 in Q3. Revenue: theatre attendance was strong in the quarter (Cinemark US attendance +12.7%; domestic box office $3.05B in Q3-26 vs a much weaker Q3-25, when JJSF itself said Q4 box office was down about 11%). Sysco US local cases rose 2.7% in Jul-Sep, so foodservice demand was not collapsing. I build revenue at roughly -2% to -3%, close to the consensus, with beverage the likely upside. Against that: diesel kept rising after the Aug 5 call (from $5.35 on Aug 3 to $6.53 on Sep 21, and $6.22 so far in FQ1-27 vs $3.72 a year earlier). Management will have to talk about a larger freight headwind in Q1 FY27, the seasonally weakest quarter and the one that cost -15% last February. The stock has also already rallied about 11% on the turnaround story. A small beat with cautious freight commentary could easily trade flat to down by 13:00. The net is a slight upward tilt that I cannot show to be unpriced.

recommendation.reason: The most likely surprise is a modest EPS beat: analysts under-called Apollo savings in Q3, and the year-ago base was flattered by tax and insurance, so the bar is soft. Strong theatre attendance should help beverage. But the market has rallied about 11% since August on exactly this story, so the beat is plausibly what the price already holds. Diesel ran well above management's August description after the call, which threatens the FY27 commentary, the line the stock has traded on in two of the last four prints. Nothing reaches 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Commentary that FQ1-27 freight and fuel costs (diesel above $6) will outrun Apollo savings, or that the return to sales growth slips past early FY27. Either would turn the call negative even on a headline EPS beat.

self_critique: The case for long: the analysts under-called Apollo by 8% in Q3 and kept Q4 near pre-call levels, so a $1.40+ print against $1.21 would be a 15%+ headline beat on a thin, three-analyst name, and the box office tailwind is real. The previous two 'beat' quarters with in-line sales went +7.7% and +1.1%. The case for short: the stock has already rallied 11% on the turnaround while the market fell. Diesel at $6+ makes FY27 freight commentary worse than in August. Q1 is the seasonally weakest quarter, and last February's Q1 commentary cost 15%. Last November a $0.34 EPS beat with a revenue miss faded from about +5% pre-market to +1.1%. With these two cases roughly balanced, I leave p_up near 50.
approach_notes: The P4 prompt to show the consensus was stale paid off: rebuilding the $1.21 from FY estimates, and the year-ago base from the tax and insurance items, turned an apparently soft bar into a modestly soft one. The 'freshest data first' rule pointed me to diesel after the call, the most useful forward datapoint. With no option chain, nothing measured what the market held, which made it hard to call anything unpriced.
